case_name: United States v. Springfield Clinic (DOJ Settlement Agreement)
court: U.S. District Court, Central District of Illinois (via DOJ settlement without trial)
docket: N/A — DOJ settlement agreement, not docketed as civil suit
claim_type: Website, patient portals, and mobile applications inaccessible to patients with visual and manual impairments; patient could not access medical records or pay bills online
outcome: DOJ settlement — $5,000 to complainant; Springfield Clinic must conform all digital properties to WCAG 2.1 AA; must hire independent web accessibility consultant within 3 months
estimated_defense_cost: DOJ enforcement investigation costs plus remediation cost of full digital accessibility overhaul (estimated $50k–$200k for a multi-platform healthcare system)

sources.name: DOJ — Justice Department Secures Agreement with Springfield Clinic (May 8, 2024)
DOJ — Springfield Clinic Settlement Agreement (full text)

summary_one_line: DOJ forced a private healthcare clinic to make its patient portal and website WCAG 2.1 AA compliant after a patient couldn't access their own medical records — healthcare digital accessibility is now a DOJ enforcement priority.
notes: Announced May 8, 2024. Part of DOJ's Tech Equity Initiative. The $5,000 payment is for complainant's damages. The real cost is the mandatory independent consultant + full remediation of website, portals, and apps to WCAG 2.1 AA. This case is ideal for healthcare client pitches. Settlement requires periodic reporting to DOJ on compliance status.
